category_title: Hospitalized youth with mental disorders exhibiting radical mood swings and behavioral instability
minimal_context: The student is continuing a long-term drawing project during an art lesson in class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's continue with your creative art work today. You can keep working on your drawing.

STUDENT: I'm making this drawing about my psychological issues. It shows how my inner world is stormy and complicated.

TUTOR: Okay, keep working on it.

STUDENT: I've been working on this long process of creative art work for weeks, but my mood is starting to swing.

TUTOR: Just do what you can with it right now.

STUDENT: No, I'm suddenly in a really bad mood. I'm abruptly throwing it away!

options.A: Use open-ended questions to guide the student in their drawing with thought-provoking questions and questions-as-suggestions.
options.B: Clarify that the suitable time for bringing up psychological issues is during psychotherapy meetings.
options.C: Smile at the student's accomplishment and gently congratulate them on the progress of the drawing.
options.D: Leave the student free to choose any format and materials they like to do the drawing.
